ui.tagline: Clay shooting for interpreters — from zero
ui.hero_p: Twelve missions to learn the language of Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting: targets and how they fly, the gun, lead and shooting technique, the FITASC rules, the referee's calls and the etiquette of the sport. Then practise as you would on a real stand: translate the coach, recognise the target, find the lead and make the referee's call.

ui.game_call_d: Real situations on the stand: what does the referee decide?
ui.game_terms_d: Match the English term with the word shooters use in your language.
ui.game_exam_d: 30 questions from all missions. Pass with 80% and get your certificate.

ui.perceived: Lead you see at the decision
ui.lab_note: Slow motion, simplified physics for teaching. The shot slows down as it flies: on average about 330 m/s over 15 m, 300 m/s over 25 m and 255 m/s over 40 m (it leaves the barrel at about 360–430 m/s). It takes about 0.15 s from the decision to the shot (an average estimate). The ring marks the part of the pattern dense enough to break the target: a radius of about 33 cm at 15 m and 45 cm at 40 m. The muzzle is about 1 m from the eye. Distances along the target's line, the lead and the ring are to scale; the target is drawn larger than life so you can see it (about to scale where the lead is counted in target widths). The actual lead depends on the target's speed, distance and angle, the cartridge and the shooter.

ui.compare: Same target, four methods: the actual lead is the same, the lead you see is not
ui.how_maintained: The muzzles wait in front and the target closes the gap. Press Shoot when the gap looks right: the gun then moves at the target's speed and holds that lead.
ui.how_swing: The muzzles start behind the target and move faster than it. Press Shoot as the muzzles pass the front of the target: the gun keeps gaining during the delay, so the actual lead is bigger.
ui.how_pullaway: The muzzles move with the target first, then accelerate ahead. Press Shoot while the gun is still accelerating: the lead you see is smaller than the actual lead.
ui.how_ambush: The muzzles wait still at a point ahead. Press Shoot before the target reaches that point: the shot needs time, so a shot fired as the target arrives goes behind.

ui.anim_h_pair: Watch how a double is thrown
ui.anim_h_call: Watch the call and the release
ui.anim_h_misfire: Watch what to do after a misfire
ui.anim_w_flight: Follow the whole flight: where the target comes from, where you see it clearly and where it goes.
ui.anim_w_points: The eyes wait at the pick-up point, the muzzles at the hold point; the target breaks at the break point.
ui.anim_w_eyes: Soft focus around the pick-up point, then hard focus on the front edge of the target.
ui.anim_w_stance: The front foot points at the break point; the body turns back to the hold point.
ui.anim_w_pair: Watch when the second target leaves: after the shot, together with the first, or from the same trap.
ui.anim_w_lead: Watch the gap between the muzzles and the target at the moment of the shot, then try it yourself.
ui.anim_w_mount: The muzzles move with the target first; the mount is finished as the shot comes.
ui.anim_w_follow: The gun keeps moving after the shot; stop it at the trigger and the shot goes behind.
ui.anim_w_call: The clock shows when the target leaves after the call or the referee's signal; a late target is a No Bird.
ui.anim_w_gunpos: In Sporting™ the stock stays below the line on the vest until the target appears.
ui.anim_w_misfire: After a misfire, stay put: gun closed and pointing down the range until the referee has checked it.
ui.anim_s_in_time: The target leaves {n} s after the signal: in time (the limit is {max} s).
ui.anim_s_late: The target leaves {n} s after the signal, later than {max} s: the referee calls “No Bird” and the target is thrown again.
ui.anim_s_manual: Released by hand: the target leaves {n} s after the call (allowed: 0 to {max} s).
ui.anim_s_sonopull: Sonopull: the microphone hears the call and the target leaves {n} s later, every time.
ui.anim_s_gun_low: Ready position: the stock touches the body below the line on the vest.
ui.anim_s_gun_mount: The target has appeared: only now does the gun come up to the shoulder.
ui.anim_s_early: Called with the gun already at the shoulder: the first time, a spoken warning and a yellow card.
ui.anim_s_click: Click: the gun did not fire.
ui.anim_s_hold: Stay where you are: gun closed and pointing down the range; do not open it or touch the safety.
ui.anim_s_repeat: First malfunction of the round: the target is thrown again.
ui.anim_s_mount_ready: Ready: the gun is low and the eyes wait for the target.
ui.anim_s_move: Move: the front hand starts the muzzles along the target's line.
ui.anim_s_mount: Mount: the stock comes up to the cheek and into the shoulder; the head stays still.
ui.anim_s_shoot: Shoot: the mount is finished as the shot comes.
ui.anim_scale: Only the shooter and the stand are to scale; the field and the target's flight are shortened.
ui.anim_h_pattern: Watch how the choke changes the pattern
ui.anim_w_pattern: A shot at a plate from 36.6 m (40 yards). Pick a choke: the tighter it is, the more shot lands in the 76 cm circle and the denser it is on the target in the centre.
ui.anim_pattern_in: In the 76 cm circle: ≈ {n}% of the shot
ui.anim_pattern_load: Simplified. 28 g of No. 7½ shot is about 370 pellets; the percentages are a guide for lead shot, and your gun and cartridge may give different ones. The target (110 mm) and the circle are to scale.
